item: The storage-events journal records the first event of a pool timeout and of a gate hold (first_seen_at) at the event, beside the kept sample, so the first bad hour no longer moves with the sample
summary: Two bundles of one process put the first bad hour of the pool at 16:00 in one and 15:00 in the other (10 of 1,575 pool timeouts kept, then 10 of 1,362): the reader took the oldest KEPT event as the onset, and the keep rule moves it. storage_events.ONSET_KINDS (gate_hold, pool_timeout) now carry first_seen_at, the at of the kind's first event ever, set under the journal lock when the event is recorded, written with the counters and read back across restarts. total is the count since it (both start at the kind's first event), so no second count is stored. A file written before the field that counted events has an UNKNOWN onset: null plus first_seen_unknown, never this process's first event. The zip budget cuts events and splits, never the onset. Bytes: the member is cut to its 125,000 slot, the two keys add 88 and the method and caveat are 66 shorter with the new sentence in them, so the fixed part grows 5,129 to 5,151; at the widest names the same 5 of 20 splits are kept with 44 bytes free (was 66), ordinary names 43,495 free. Mutants: onset read off the sample, reset on every record, not persisted, new process overriding the file, legacy taking the new first event, junk accepted, no reason, every kind carrying it, onset cut with the events, reason on an empty kind: all killed.
